name: Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: €11M. Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture, Finnish National Gallery.
watch: State museum funded solely by national culture money; has an ethical gift policy.

name: Kim? Contemporary Art Centre
funding: Latvian Ministry of Culture, State Culture Capital Foundation, Riga City Council, Altum and EU social-entrepreneurship co-financing; project supporters KRASO, Kokmuiža and Media Port.
watch: Absolut and Valmiermuiža from the first text are not on its homepage. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Kim? names its two board members and posts its statutes, but no annual report, accounts or sponsor list; shows carry their own supporter credits.

name: Kin ArtStudio
funding: Small artist-run residency (active 2024); housed in the TEXAF concession, with Pro Helvetia residencies and Fondation Montresso partnership.
watch: Residency and studio founded 2011 by Vitshois Mwilambwe Bondo in a former TEXAF textile hangar. Linked to the Congo Biennale.
records_note: No Kin ArtStudio site could be opened; one interview names only Fondation Montresso as partner, and the founder funds it from art sales.

name: KIOSK
funding: Project support from Schleich-Lentz Foundation and Konschthal Esch.
records_note: Its site shows no reports or accounts; three funders appear as logos with no date, and the Kunstensite vzw board of seven is named.

name: Kiosko Galería
location: Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia
funding: Arts Collaboratory, Prince Claus Fund, independent cultural foundation; non-profit artist initiative.
watch: Independent contemporary art space and international residency in Bolivia; a non-commercial public trust.

name: Kistefos
funding: Christen Sveaas, his investment company Kistefos AS and Christen Sveaas' art foundation; Riksantikvaren, local and county councils and savings-bank foundations.
watch: Sculpture park and museum in Jevnaker featuring 'The Twist' by BIG.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2010 to 2025 with full accounts and names funders; the site names only the board chair, the register the rest.

name: Kling & Bang
funding: Icelandic Visual Arts Fund (Myndlistarsjóður), City of Reykjavík, artist members; independent artist-run collective.

name: Kölnischer Kunstverein
funding: City of Cologne Department of Art and Culture, Kunststiftung NRW; member-supported non-profit association.

name: Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum
funding: Regional state (Voronezh Oblast); director Yulia Zaichenko; partners named are other state museums.
watch: Voronezh's independent VCCA lost its premises in 2019.
records_note: It posts yearly reports 2020 to 2024 and annual financial plans 2022 to 2025, but names no funders and shows no board.

name: Kropka (Belarusian community space; listed in place of 'Krokva')
funding: Grants from unnamed international foundations cover about two-thirds of costs; visitor donations; one paid coordinator funded by donor organisations
watch: Opened Mar 2022 in Sololaki by Belarusian activists who fled repression: 700+ events and 5,000+ visitors, free coworking, screenings, language clubs and support groups. It keeps a deliberately low profile under Georgia's foreign-agent law.
records_note: No site, reports, accounts, funder list or board were found for Kropka, and press says the Tbilisi space closed in January 2025.

name: Künstlerhaus Stuttgart
funding: City of Stuttgart Cultural Office, State of Baden-Württemberg; artist-run non-profit association.
